name: Camille Breen
life: “I still remember refusing a message I couldn't deliver with a clear conscience.” People around Tideline Market know Camille by a small Sunday habit. Camille picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I was jailed for something else and shared a cell with the man she named. I won't carry messages between them.
appearance: Camille has auburn hair cut square at the nape, an aquiline nose and a square chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a washed violet jersey. It usually goes with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. When somebody else has the floor, Camille counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Camille treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Camille lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To keep the home visit clear of prison messages.
family: Lina Carbone is Camille’s older cousin. Camille chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Lina brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The absent signature*, Lina says, “I was the last person she called. The message was about soup, and its ordinariness is why I kept it.”
connections: Basil Hunter. A shopkeeper offering personal observations meets someone refusing to carry another man's messages.

reactions.situation: The witness runs into a convicted neighbor's family
reactions.response: Camille gives both parties the space to pass or speak without an audience.
